Pharma Associations.url_match_title: Pratap Group Celebrated the Grand Inauguration of Two Advanced Manufacturing Units in Pithampur - PNN Digital
Pharma Associations.content:
Pithampur (Madhya Pradesh) [India], August 21:
Pratap Group successfully inaugurated and dedicated to the nation two state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities in Madhya Pradesh. The landmark ceremony was graced by the presence of
Hon’ble Dr. Mohan Yadav, Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh
, and
Hon’ble Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture & Tourism, Government of India
, who jointly inaugurated the facilities.
The first facility,
Corsis Industries – Advanced Optical Fibre Manufacturing Plant
, was established to strengthen India’s rapidly expanding digital infrastructure. This world-class unit began manufacturing advanced optical fiber to support broadband connectivity, 5G networks, FTTH, data centers, smart cities, defense, and other critical communication systems. The plant embodied the vision of
Digital India, Make in India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat
.
The second facility,
Voltters Technologies – Advanced Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Lithium ion Battery Manufacturing Facility
, was inaugurated as a cutting edge unit equipped with modern robotic technology and Industry 4.0 automation. It commenced production of BESS and Lithium ion battery solutions, playing a pivotal role in integrating renewable energy, supporting utilities, and meeting the growing demand for commercial and industrial applications. The facility aligned with
India’s National Clean Energy Mission, Green Energy Goals, and the Developed India @2047 vision
.
Chairman and Managing Director of Pratap Group, Mr. Devendra Singh Shekhawat said
–
“I begin by expressing my heartfelt gratitude to my parents for instilling such noble values in me. It is a matter of immense pride to fulfill and carry forward the dream of my father, Thakur Pratap Singh Ji. Today is not merely an inauguration, but a day that marks a new direction for India’s bright future, clean energy, and advanced technology. With the launch of our Battery Energy Storage Systems and Advanced Optical Fibre facilities, we celebrate both pride and joy. I extend my deepest thanks to Hon’ble Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav Ji and my elder brother Shri Gajendra Singh Ji for gracing us with their presence, blessings, and encouragement.”
Mr. Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture & Tourism, said
,
“We stand at the threshold of the digital and AI era, where advanced technologies will play a pivotal role in India’s growth. Reliable power supply and high level connectivity are essential, and optical fibre and storage systems will bridge this gap, enabling secure harnessing of solar and wind energy. With an investment of nearly ₹850 crore, this plant has already created direct and indirect employment for 800–1000 people. This initiative strengthens Madhya Pradesh’s industrial growth, resource security, and infrastructure, making it a land of immense opportunities.
Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav said
–
“I am truly delighted to witness the inauguration of these advanced facilities in Madhya Pradesh. This initiative reflects the vision of clean energy, modern technology, and industrial growth that our state is committed to. I warmly congratulate the Pratap Group on their remarkable contribution and on investing in our state’s future. The creation of employment opportunities and skill development for our youth is commendable. I urge the Pratap Group to continue bringing more such investments to Madhya Pradesh, as together we can strengthen our economy, empower our people, and make our state a hub of innovation and opportunity.”
These projects are expected to generate
more than 3,500 direct and indirect employment opportunities
. Alongside, the Group has set up a training academy to nurture skills and prepare the workforce for emerging sectors.
Pratap Digital Communications Pvt. Ltd. at Unit 40
is dedicated to optical fiber cable manufacturing under the brand name
Corsis Technologies
, with an annual production capacity of approximately
6.5 million fiberkilometers
and an advanced R&D Centre.
Corsis Industries at Unit 98
, spread over
8,067 square meters
, has an annual capacity of
5.5 million fiberkilometers
, with products serving broadband, 5G, FTTH, data centers, smart cities, defense, and other strategic communication infrastructure.
Voltters Technologies at Unit 100
, spread over
20,505 square meters
, is a fully automated and robotic plant with a production capacity of
3 GWh
, developed to manufacture Battery Energy Storage Systems and Lithium ion Battery solutions.
If you object to the content of this press release, please notify us at
[email protected]
. We will respond and rectify the situation within 24 hours.

Heranba Industries
reported a consolidated net profit of
₹7.03 crore
for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, marking a 57% increase year-on-year and a sharp recovery from the previous quarter’s loss.
The agrochemical manufacturer’s revenue from operations rose 19% year-on-year to
₹383.20 crore
, supported by stronger domestic sales which accounted for nearly 80% of total segment revenue.
The Board of Directors approved the unaudited financial results on August 22, 2026, alongside an investment plan for its wholly owned subsidiary, Mikusu India Private Limited.
Financial Performance
Consolidated revenue from operations stood at ₹383.20 crore in Q1FY27, up from ₹452.43 crore in Q1FY26 but significantly higher than the ₹319.48 crore recorded in Q4FY26. The company returned to profitability after posting a consolidated loss of ₹58.32 crore in the previous quarter.

Standalone results showed a net profit of ₹9.46 crore for the quarter, compared to a loss of ₹12.50 crore in Q4FY26 and a profit of ₹22.02 crore in Q1FY26. Standalone revenue was ₹364.99 crore.
What the Numbers Show
A significant divergence exists between standalone and consolidated tax treatments. While standalone operations generated a pre-tax profit of ₹13.41 crore with a modest tax expense of ₹3.95 crore, the consolidated group reported a higher pre-tax profit of ₹20.10 crore but incurred a substantially larger tax expense of ₹13.07 crore. This elevated consolidated tax burden, driven largely by a deferred tax charge of ₹8.92 crore, reduced the bottom-line impact of the operational turnaround, resulting in a lower consolidated net profit relative to the standalone figure.
Corporate Developments
The Board approved an investment of up to
₹25 crore
in the share capital of Mikusu India Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, through a right issue. The transaction is described as being undertaken in the ordinary course of business at arm's length.
Mikusu India, incorporated on April 9, 2022, is engaged in the trading of agrochemical products. It reported a turnover of
₹182.68 crore
as on March 31, 2026, up from ₹152.40 crore in FY25 and ₹92.91 crore in FY24. The investment aims to support the business operations and growth plans of the subsidiary. There will be no change in Heranba Industries’ shareholding structure, as it will continue to hold 100% of the share capital.
Additionally, Mr. Punit H. Vyas, currently serving as Quality Control - Head, has been designated as Senior Management Personnel effective August 22, 2026.

Demineralizing Resins Market Demand to Accelerate by 2035 on Stricter Water Quality Standards
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Demineralizing Resins market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global demineralizing resins market is entering a period of sustained expansion, with demand projected to rise at a compound annual growth rate of 4-6% from 2026 to 2035. This growth is underpinned by the essential role of ion-exchange polymers in producing high-purity water for power generation, pharmaceutical manufacturing, microelectronics fabrication, and food processing. As environmental regulations tighten and industrial processes demand ever-higher water quality, the replacement cycle for mixed-bed and layered resin systems remains a stable base load, accounting for roughly 60-70% of annual purchases. High-purity and specialty grades, already representing an estimated 25-35% of market value, are expected to gain further share as semiconductor and bioprocessing specifications become more stringent. Supply remains concentrated among a dozen global manufacturers, with lead times for certified high-purity resins extending 8-16 weeks and occasional spot shortages during peak maintenance periods. Raw material price volatility, particularly for styrene and divinylbenzene, continues to influence contract pricing, while supplier qualification barriers protect incumbents. This report provides a data-driven analysis of market size, demand structure, supply capability, trade flows, pricing, and competitive landscape, offering a transparent forecast to 2035 for manufacturers, distributors, and investors.
The baseline scenario for the demineralizing resins market points to steady growth through 2035, with global consumption rising from an estimated 2025 base to a market index of 160 by 2035 (2025=100). This corresponds to a CAGR of 4.8%, reflecting robust demand from industrial water treatment, power generation, and high-purity applications. The recurring replacement cycle for standard mixed-bed resins—typically every 3-5 years—provides a predictable demand floor, while new capacity additions in semiconductor fabs, pharmaceutical bioprocessing, and advanced chemical plants drive incremental growth. High-purity and specialty grades are expected to outpace functional grades, supported by tightening quality standards in electronics and clinical applications. Supply-side constraints, including the concentration of production among a dozen global players and the 12-24 month validation period for new suppliers, will keep pricing firm for certified products. Regional import dependence in Latin America, the Middle East, and Africa will sustain trade flows from Europe, North America, and Asia. Raw material cost volatility remains a key margin risk, but quarterly contract adjustments and premium pricing for differentiated products mitigate impact. Overall, the market is set for balanced growth, with opportunities in emerging markets and specialty segments.

Primary Demand Drivers
Expanding industrial water treatment requirements amid stricter effluent discharge regulations
Growing demand for high-purity water in semiconductor and microelectronics manufacturing
Rising pharmaceutical and bioprocessing needs for validated demineralization media

Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Industrial Water Treatment (estimated share: 35%)
Industrial water treatment remains the largest end-use segment, accounting for roughly 35% of global demineralizing resin demand. This segment includes boiler feedwater treatment, cooling water makeup, and process water purification across chemical, petrochemical, and manufacturing facilities. The demand mechanism is driven by the need to prevent scale formation, corrosion, and fouling in boilers and heat exchangers, which directly impacts operational efficiency and equipment lifespan. As environmental regulations tighten, particularly in Asia and Europe, industrial operators are increasingly adopting demineralization systems to meet effluent quality standards and enable water recycling. The replacement cycle for mixed-bed resins in this segment is typically 3-5 years, creating a stable base load. Through 2035, growth will be supported by industrial expansion in emerging markets, retrofitting of aging water treatment infrastructure, and the push for zero-liquid discharge in water-stressed regions. Key demand-side indicators include industrial production indices, capital expenditure in chemical and petrochemical plants, and regulatory enforcement of water quality standards. Current trend: Steady growth driven by stricter discharge standards and water reuse initiatives.
Major trends:
Shift toward higher cross-link density resins for improved kinetics and longer service life, Adoption of monodisperse bead technologies to reduce pressure drop and improve regeneration efficiency, Integration of demineralization with membrane systems for hybrid treatment trains, and Growing use of resin regeneration services to extend media life and reduce waste.
Representative participants:
Dow Inc, Lanxess AG, Purolite Corporation, Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation, and Thermax Limited.
Power Generation (estimated share: 20%)
Power generation is a critical end-use sector for demineralizing resins, representing about 20% of global demand. The primary application is the production of ultra-pure water for boiler feedwater and steam generation in thermal, nuclear, and combined-cycle power plants. Demineralizing resins remove dissolved ions to prevent scale formation, corrosion, and turbine fouling, which are major causes of efficiency losses and unplanned outages. The demand mechanism is tied to the capacity factor of power plants and the frequency of resin replacement, typically every 2-5 years depending on water quality and operating conditions. As global electricity demand rises, particularly in Asia and the Middle East, new power plant construction and the refurbishment of aging facilities will drive resin consumption. Nuclear power, with its stringent water purity requirements, is a particularly stable and high-value segment. Through 2035, the transition toward higher-efficiency supercritical and ultra-supercritical coal plants, as well as the growth of nuclear capacity in China and India, will support demand. Key indicators include power generation capacity additions, plant utilization rates, and maintenance schedules. Current trend: Moderate growth amid nuclear and thermal capacity additions and aging plant maintenance.
Major trends:
Increasing use of high-purity grade resins for nuclear and supercritical boiler applications, Development of resins with higher oxidation resistance for demanding operating conditions, Adoption of online monitoring and automated regeneration to optimize resin life, and Growing focus on reducing chemical regeneration waste and improving sustainability.
Representative participants:
Dow Inc, Lanxess AG, Purolite Corporation, Evoqua Water Technologies, and Ion Exchange (India) Ltd.
Pharmaceutical & Bioprocessing (estimated share: 15%)
The pharmaceutical and bioprocessing sector accounts for approximately 15% of demineralizing resin demand, but it is the fastest-growing segment due to the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and the increasing stringency of regulatory requirements. Demineralizing resins are used to produce water for injection (WFI), purification of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), and in chromatography and ion-exchange processes for protein purification. The demand mechanism is driven by the need for consistent, validated water quality that meets pharmacopeia standards (USP, EP, JP). Resins used in this segment must undergo rigorous qualification and validation, with supplier change requiring 12-24 months of testing and documentation. As the biopharmaceutical industry grows, particularly in the production of monoclonal antibodies and cell therapies, the demand for high-purity and specialty resins will rise. The trend toward continuous manufacturing and single-use technologies also influences resin specifications. Through 2035, growth will be supported by increasing R&D investment, the expansion of biosimilar production, and the localization of pharmaceutical manufacturing in emerging markets. Key indicators include biopharmaceutical pipeline activity, regulatory approvals, and capital expenditure in manufacturing facilities. Current trend: Fastest-growing segment driven by biopharmaceutical manufacturing and stringent purity standards.
Major trends:
Rising demand for high-purity grade resins with low extractables and consistent performance, Adoption of single-use and disposable ion-exchange devices in bioprocessing, Increasing use of mixed-bed resins for final polishing in WFI systems, and Growing emphasis on resin lifetime and regeneration protocols to reduce costs.
Representative participants:
Purolite Corporation, Dow Inc, Lanxess AG, Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation, and Novasep.
Electronics & Semiconductors (estimated share: 15%)
The electronics and semiconductor sector represents about 15% of global demineralizing resin demand, with high-purity grades being essential for producing ultra-pure water (UPW) used in wafer fabrication, cleaning, and etching processes. As semiconductor manufacturing nodes shrink and chip complexity increases, the required water purity levels become more stringent, with resistivity approaching 18.2 MΩ·cm and total organic carbon (TOC) in the parts-per-billion range. Demineralizing resins, particularly mixed-bed and polishing grades, are critical for achieving these specifications. The demand mechanism is tied to the capital expenditure cycle of semiconductor fabs, with each new fab requiring significant quantities of resin for initial fill and ongoing replacement. The global semiconductor market is projected to grow at a high single-digit rate through 2035, driven by AI, IoT, and 5G applications, which will directly boost resin demand. Additionally, the trend toward localized chip manufacturing in the US, Europe, and Asia-Pacific will create new demand centers. Key indicators include semiconductor fab construction announcements, wafer starts, and technology node transitions. Current trend: Strong growth driven by semiconductor fab expansion and ultra-pure water requirements.
Major trends:
Development of ultra-high-purity resins with minimal ionic and organic leachables, Increasing use of monodisperse resins for improved rinse-up times and lower TOC, Adoption of advanced regeneration and polishing systems to maintain water quality, and Growing demand for specialty resins in advanced packaging and MEMS fabrication.
Representative participants:
Dow Inc, Lanxess AG, Purolite Corporation, Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation, and ResinTech Inc.
Food & Beverage (estimated share: 15%)
The food and beverage sector accounts for approximately 15% of demineralizing resin demand, with applications including sugar decolorization, juice clarification, wine stabilization, and process water treatment. Demineralizing resins are used to remove unwanted ions, colors, and impurities from liquid food products, improving quality and shelf life. The demand mechanism is driven by consumer preferences for clean-label products and the need for consistent product quality. In sugar refining, ion-exchange resins are essential for decolorization and demineralization of syrups, while in the beverage industry, they are used to adjust water chemistry for optimal taste and stability. The sector is also seeing increased adoption of resin-based processes for the recovery of valuable by-products and the reduction of waste. Through 2035, growth will be supported by the expansion of processed food consumption in emerging markets, the trend toward natural and organic products, and the need for water conservation in food processing. Key indicators include food production volumes, sugar and beverage output, and regulatory standards for food safety and quality. Current trend: Steady growth driven by product purification and process water treatment.
Major trends:
Increasing use of food-grade resins with FDA and EU compliance, Adoption of continuous ion-exchange systems for higher efficiency and lower chemical usage, Growing demand for resins in plant-based beverage and alternative protein processing, and Focus on reducing water and energy consumption in food processing operations.
Representative participants:
Dow Inc, Lanxess AG, Purolite Corporation, Mitsubishi Chemical Corporation, and Thermax Limited.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 45%)
Asia-Pacific leads global demand, driven by rapid industrialization, power generation expansion, and semiconductor manufacturing growth in China, Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan. The region also hosts major resin production capacity, with local players expanding. Water scarcity and stricter environmental regulations are boosting adoption of demineralization systems. Growth is supported by infrastructure investments and the relocation of high-tech manufacturing. Direction: Dominant and fastest-growing.
North America (estimated share: 25%)
North America is a mature market with steady demand from power generation, pharmaceuticals, and food processing. The US is a major producer and consumer, with a strong focus on high-purity grades for semiconductor and bioprocessing applications. The reshoring of semiconductor manufacturing and investments in water infrastructure are expected to support growth. Replacement demand remains a key driver. Direction: Stable with moderate growth.
Europe (estimated share: 20%)
Europe has a well-established market, with demand driven by stringent environmental regulations, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and industrial water treatment. The region is home to several leading resin producers and has a strong focus on sustainability and circular economy initiatives. Growth is moderate but stable, with opportunities in specialty grades and water reuse projects. Direction: Mature with steady demand.
Latin America (estimated share: 5%)
Latin America is a small but growing market, heavily reliant on imports from Europe and North America. Demand is driven by mining, food and beverage, and municipal water treatment. Economic volatility and infrastructure gaps pose challenges, but increasing investment in water treatment and industrial development offers growth potential. Local manufacturing is limited, creating opportunities for distributors. Direction: Emerging with high import dependence.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 5%)
The Middle East and Africa are emerging markets with significant demand for desalination and water treatment due to water scarcity. The region relies almost entirely on imports, with distributors playing a critical role. Power generation and petrochemical industries are key consumers. Investments in water infrastructure and industrial diversification are expected to drive growth, albeit from a low base. Direction: Growing with water scarcity focus.

Scotland's industrial biotechnology sector is set to receive further support with the launch of a new competition aimed at helping bio-based innovations bridge the gap between laboratory research and commercial production.
The Industrial Biotechnology Innovation Centre (IBioIC) has opened applications for its BioProcess Scale-up Accelerator Competition, offering up to £10,000 towards project costs for companies and academic teams using its FlexBIO facility at Heriot-Watt University.
The competition is intended to address one of the persistent challenges facing industrial biotechnology: translating a promising laboratory process into a manufacturing process that can operate reliably at a commercially relevant scale.
Backed by Scottish Government funding, the initiative builds on the
launch
last year of Scotland's first open-access 300-litre fermenter. The facility allows organisations to test and validate bioprocesses at larger volumes without the capital investment required to develop their own specialist infrastructure.
Projects supported through the competition can range from bench-scale work through to production at 300 litres, helping organisations prepare processes for manufacturing, customer trials and future investment.
Neil Renault, director of bioprocessing scale-up at FlexBIO (pictured right), said: "Scaling up isn't just about making more product. Every process behaves differently as volumes increase, so it's essential to understand how fermentation, downstream processing and product recovery perform at scale before making further investment."
One company already using the facility is HydRegen, a University of Oxford spinout developing enzyme-based technology intended to replace heavy metal catalysts used in chemical manufacturing.
HydRegen needed to produce a larger quantity of enzyme for a demonstration with an industrial manufacturing partner than it could generate in-house. Working with FlexBIO, the company transferred an established five-litre laboratory process to the 300-litre fermenter, producing material at a 200-litre working volume.
The project also generated data on how the process performed during scale-up and demonstrated that HydRegen's fermentation strategy could be maintained at the larger volume.
Renault said the experience illustrated the role specialist infrastructure could play in helping companies move beyond the laboratory.
"Access to infrastructure can provide not only the quantities of material businesses need, but also the process data and confidence required to take the next step towards commercial manufacturing," he said.
Dr Matthew Hodges, chief operating officer at HydRegen, said access to the facility and technical expertise had enabled the company to demonstrate its technology at a larger scale and provided greater confidence as it moved towards commercialisation.
The BioProcess Scale-up Accelerator Competition is open to industry and academic-led projects with a credible route to market and plans to secure follow-on investment.
Successful projects must be completed by the end of March 2027 and demonstrate how they could contribute to Scotland's bio-based manufacturing sector through areas including business growth, investment, collaborative R&D or strengthened supply chains.
Applications close on 1 September 2026.

Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Semiconductor and Precision Manufacturing (estimated share: 35%)
This segment is the largest consumer of glove port inserts, driven by the relentless expansion of semiconductor fabrication facilities worldwide. Advanced-node logic and memory chips require ultra-clean environments, and isolators equipped with glove port inserts are critical for operator intervention without breaking contamination control. The demand is tied to both new fab construction and the retrofitting of existing facilities to meet stricter cleanroom standards. Through 2035, the segment will see sustained growth as leading-edge fabs in Taiwan, South Korea, the US, and Europe increase capacity. Replacement cycles are shorter here due to high utilization rates and aggressive chemical exposure, with inserts often replaced every 12-18 months. Demand-side indicators include fab capex announcements, wafer starts, and cleanroom certification frequency. The trend toward integrated systems with sensors is particularly strong in this segment, as fabs seek to reduce unplanned downtime and extend mean time between replacements. Major players in this segment include semiconductor equipment OEMs and specialty component suppliers who must meet rigorous material and dimensional specifications. Current trend: Dominant and growing with fab expansion.
Major trends:
Adoption of integrated sensor-enabled glove port inserts for real-time monitoring, Shift to higher chemical resistance materials for aggressive etch and clean processes, Increased use of automation and robotics reducing manual intervention frequency, and Localization of supply chains to reduce lead times and import dependence.
Representative participants:
Terra Universal, Clean Air Products, Isotech Design, Kemp Company, and Esco Micro Pte. Ltd.
Electronics and Optical Systems (estimated share: 25%)
Electronics and optical systems manufacturing, including advanced packaging, printed circuit board assembly, and display panel production, relies on glove port inserts to maintain cleanroom integrity during manual handling and inspection. The growth of 5G infrastructure, IoT devices, and augmented reality optics is driving demand for precision assembly in controlled environments. This segment is characterized by a mix of standard and premium inserts, with a growing preference for consumables that offer longer service life to minimize downtime in high-throughput lines. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the expansion of advanced packaging facilities, particularly in Asia-Pacific, where OSATs (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) are investing heavily. The demand story is also linked to the miniaturization of electronic components, which increases the risk of contamination and necessitates more frequent replacement of glove port inserts. Key demand indicators include electronics production indices, cleanroom area under management, and the number of assembly lines requiring isolator access. The trend toward integrated systems is less pronounced here compared to semiconductors, but there is growing interest in inserts with antimicrobial coatings and static-dissipative properties to protect sensitive components. Current trend: Steady growth with advanced packaging and display manufacturing.
Major trends:
Growth of advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration driving cleanroom demand, Adoption of static-dissipative and antimicrobial insert materials, Increased use of glove port inserts in inspection and testing stations, and Shift toward modular and quick-change insert designs for faster line changeovers.
Representative participants:
Labconco, NuAire, Esco Micro Pte. Ltd, Getinge AB, and SKAN AG.
Industrial Automation and Instrumentation (estimated share: 20%)
Industrial automation and instrumentation applications, including chemical processing, pharmaceutical production, and food and beverage handling, use glove port inserts in isolators and glove boxes to protect operators from hazardous substances and maintain product purity. This segment is driven by the need for safe handling of potent compounds and the increasing automation of manual processes. While automation reduces the frequency of manual intervention, the installed base of isolators continues to grow, and replacement inserts are needed for maintenance and upgrades. Through 2035, the segment will see steady demand as industries adopt stricter safety regulations and seek to improve operator ergonomics. The trend is toward inserts with enhanced chemical resistance and longer service intervals, reducing total cost of ownership. Demand indicators include industrial production indices, chemical industry output, and the number of isolator installations in process plants. The adoption of integrated systems with sensors is slower in this segment due to cost sensitivity, but there is growing interest in inserts that can be sterilized in place (SIP) and withstand repeated autoclaving. Major companies in this segment include isolator manufacturers and specialty component suppliers that offer validated solutions for pharmaceutical and chemical applications. Current trend: Moderate growth with automation and process control upgrades.
Major trends:
Increasing use of glove port inserts in pharmaceutical isolators for potent compound handling, Demand for SIP-compatible and autoclavable insert materials, Integration of RFID tags for tracking replacement cycles and inventory management, and Growth of modular isolator designs that simplify insert replacement.
Representative participants:
Getinge AB, SKAN AG, Comecer S.p.A, Extract Technology, and Burkert Fluid Control Systems.
OEM Integration and Maintenance (estimated share: 15%)
OEM integration and maintenance represents the aftermarket channel where glove port inserts are supplied as original equipment on new isolators and as replacement parts during service and maintenance. This segment is closely tied to the production of isolators and glove boxes by major equipment manufacturers, who source inserts from specialized suppliers. The demand is driven by the global sales of new isolators, which are expected to grow in line with cleanroom construction and pharmaceutical capacity expansion. Additionally, maintenance contracts and service agreements create recurring demand for replacement inserts, often with specified intervals. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the trend toward longer equipment lifecycles and the need for periodic replacement of wear parts. OEMs are increasingly partnering with insert manufacturers to develop integrated systems that offer better performance and easier maintenance. Demand indicators include isolator production volumes, service contract penetration, and the average age of installed equipment. The competitive landscape is characterized by long-term supply agreements and the need for rigorous qualification to meet OEM specifications. Major companies in this segment include both insert manufacturers and isolator OEMs that offer in-house replacement parts. Current trend: Stable growth with OEM partnerships and aftermarket services.
Major trends:
Long-term supply agreements between insert manufacturers and isolator OEMs, Growth of service contracts and preventive maintenance programs, Development of OEM-specific insert designs for proprietary isolator models, and Increasing use of digital platforms for ordering and inventory management.
Representative participants:
Terra Universal, Clean Air Products, Isotech Design, Kemp Company, Labconco, and NuAire.
Pharmaceutical and Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing (estimated share: 5%)
Pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturing, while a smaller share of the glove port inserts market, is a high-growth segment driven by the expansion of biologics, cell and gene therapy, and personalized medicine. These applications require isolators with glove port inserts to maintain aseptic conditions during drug product filling and handling. The demand is characterized by a preference for premium inserts with high chemical resistance and compatibility with aggressive cleaning agents like hydrogen peroxide vapor. Through 2035, the segment will see above-average growth as new biopharmaceutical facilities are built, particularly in North America and Europe, and as existing facilities upgrade to meet stricter regulatory standards. The trend is toward integrated systems with sensors that monitor glove integrity and contamination events, aligning with the industry's focus on quality by design. Demand indicators include biopharmaceutical pipeline approvals, facility construction announcements, and regulatory inspection frequency. The segment is relatively small but offers high margins and long-term contracts, making it attractive for specialized suppliers. Major companies in this segment include isolator manufacturers and component suppliers with validated solutions for aseptic processing. Current trend: Emerging growth with biologics and cell therapy expansion.
Major trends:
Expansion of cell and gene therapy manufacturing requiring isolator-based containment, Adoption of single-use technologies that integrate glove port inserts, Increased focus on glove integrity testing and real-time monitoring, and Regulatory push for contamination control in aseptic processing.
Representative participants:
Getinge AB, SKAN AG, Comecer S.p.A, Extract Technology, and Esco Micro Pte. Ltd.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 55%)
Asia-Pacific leads the glove port inserts market, driven by semiconductor fab construction in Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China. The region accounts for the majority of global output and consumption, with strong demand from electronics and precision manufacturing. Growth is supported by government incentives for chip production and expanding cleanroom capacity. Through 2035, the region will maintain its dominance, with China emerging as a key consumer and producer. Direction: Dominant and fastest-growing.
North America (estimated share: 20%)
North America is a significant market, driven by semiconductor fab expansion under the CHIPS Act and a strong pharmaceutical sector. Import dependence remains high, but onshoring efforts are gradually increasing domestic production. The region is a leader in adopting integrated sensor-based inserts, supported by a focus on operational efficiency. Growth will be steady, with demand from advanced packaging and biopharmaceutical manufacturing. Direction: Steady growth with onshoring initiatives.
Europe (estimated share: 15%)
Europe's glove port inserts market is supported by a robust pharmaceutical industry and cleanroom standards. The region is a net importer, with domestic production meeting less than half of demand. Regulatory divergence across EU member states adds compliance costs, but the push for localized semiconductor manufacturing and green transitions is creating new opportunities. Growth will be moderate, with emphasis on premium and integrated products. Direction: Moderate growth with regulatory focus.
Latin America (estimated share: 5%)
Latin America is a small but growing market, driven by pharmaceutical manufacturing and electronics assembly in Mexico and Brazil. The region relies heavily on imports, and demand is sensitive to economic cycles. Investments in cleanroom infrastructure for medical devices and food processing are expected to drive moderate growth through 2035. The market is price-sensitive, favoring standard inserts over premium grades. Direction: Emerging growth with industrial diversification.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 5%)
The Middle East & Africa region has a nascent glove port inserts market, with demand from pharmaceutical manufacturing and oil & gas laboratories. The region imports most of its requirements, and growth is tied to healthcare infrastructure investments and industrial diversification. The market is small but offers opportunities for suppliers willing to navigate local regulations and establish distribution networks. Growth is expected to be gradual. Direction: Niche growth with healthcare and oil & gas.

Modular Screen Units Market to Reach USD 4.3B by 2035 on Mining Replacement Demand
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Modular Screen Units market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global Modular Screen Units market is entering a period of sustained expansion, with demand increasingly tied to the replacement cycles of vibrating screens across mineral processing, aggregate production, and recycling operations. These pre-fabricated, reconfigurable display panels—comprising polyurethane, rubber, and hybrid steel-frame modules—are essential consumables that directly influence throughput, wear life, and operational uptime. In 2026, the market is estimated to be valued at approximately USD 2.8 billion, with modular panels representing 55–65% of new unit shipments by value, a share that is expected to climb further as operators prioritize longer-lasting media and reduced downtime. The shift from traditional woven wire and perforated metal to advanced polymer-based modules is a defining trend, supported by environmental regulations that favor quieter, lower-vibration screening solutions. Digital procurement platforms and standardized connector interfaces are compressing lead times from 12–16 weeks to 8–10 weeks for standard sizes, reshaping the competitive landscape. However, raw material price volatility for polyurethane precursors and abrasion-grade rubber, along with lengthy qualification cycles in safety-critical environments, remain structural challenges. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of market size, demand architecture, supply structure, trade flows, pricing, and competitive positioning, with a forecast horizon extending to 2035. It is designed for manufacturers, distributors, importers, investors, and strategy teams seeking a data-driven view of this specialized industrial consumables market.
The baseline scenario for the Modular Screen Units market points to a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 4.8% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching 155 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by the ongoing expansion of global mining and aggregates output, particularly in emerging economies, and the accelerating adoption of modular polyurethane and rubber screens that offer 2–3 times longer wear life compared to traditional steel decks. Replacement cycles, typically ranging from 4 to 12 months depending on material abrasiveness, create a recurring demand stream that is less sensitive to capital expenditure cycles than full machine purchases. The market is also benefiting from the trend toward hybrid modular designs, which combine steel frames with polymer wear surfaces, growing at 8–12% annually as operators seek a balance between throughput and media life. Digital procurement and standardized interfaces are reducing lead times, narrowing the advantage of local distributors and enabling more efficient global sourcing. However, the baseline forecast assumes no major disruptions from raw material shortages or trade policy shifts; it incorporates moderate price increases of 2–3% per year for polymer-based modules. The competitive landscape remains concentrated, with the top 6–8 global producers accounting for 65–75% of output by volume, but import-dependent markets in Africa, Latin America, and parts of Asia will continue to rely on cross-border sourcing, creating opportunities for regional distributors and new entrants that can navigate qualification hurdles.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
Rising global mining output and ore processing volumes
Growing aggregates demand from infrastructure and construction
Replacement cycle demand from installed vibrating screen base
Shift to polyurethane and rubber modular panels for longer wear life
Environmental regulations on noise and vibration in quarries and mines
Digital procurement platforms reducing lead times and transaction costs
Potential Growth Constraints
Raw material cost volatility for polyurethane precursors and abrasion-grade rubber
Lengthy qualification cycles (3–9 months) in safety-critical mining environments
Logistics inefficiencies for oversized bulk shipments, especially to landlocked regions
Competition from alternative screening media such as woven wire and perforated plate
Economic slowdowns in key mining regions affecting capital and maintenance budgets
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Mining and Mineral Processing (estimated share: 45%)
In mining and mineral processing, modular screen units are critical for classifying ore and removing oversize material. The segment is driven by the need to maximize throughput while minimizing downtime. Replacement cycles are short, often 4–12 months, depending on ore abrasiveness. Through 2035, demand will be supported by the expansion of copper, gold, and iron ore mining, particularly in Chile, Peru, Australia, and Africa. The shift to polyurethane and rubber panels, which offer 2–3 times longer wear life than steel, is accelerating as operators seek to reduce maintenance costs. Digital monitoring and predictive maintenance are becoming standard, allowing operators to optimize screen media replacement schedules. Key demand indicators include global mining capex, ore grades, and commodity prices. Major players in this segment include Polydeck, Tega, Multotec, and FLSmidth, which supply modular systems that integrate with existing vibrating screens. Current trend: Increasing adoption of polyurethane and rubber modular panels for high-wear applications.
Major trends:
Shift to polyurethane and rubber panels for longer wear life, Adoption of hybrid modular designs for high-impact applications, Integration of IoT sensors for real-time screen performance monitoring, and Growing use of modular panels in coarse and fine screening applications.
Representative participants:
Polydeck Screen Corporation, Tega Industries Limited, Multotec Group, FLSmidth (Ludowici), and Sandvik AB.
Aggregates and Construction (estimated share: 30%)
The aggregates segment is a major consumer of modular screen units, used in quarries to produce graded materials for concrete, asphalt, and road base. Growth is tied to infrastructure investment, urbanization, and construction activity. As governments worldwide increase spending on roads, bridges, and housing, the demand for aggregates rises, directly boosting screen media consumption. Modular panels are favored for their quick installation and reduced downtime, which is critical in high-volume quarry operations. The trend toward recycling construction and demolition waste is also creating new demand, as operators use modular screens to separate materials. By 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a steady pace, supported by the need for higher-quality aggregates and stricter specifications. Key indicators include construction spending, housing starts, and government infrastructure budgets. Major companies supplying this segment include Metso, Sandvik, and Haver & Boecker, which offer modular screen systems that enhance screening efficiency. Current trend: Rising infrastructure spending drives demand for modular screens in crushing and screening plants.
Major trends:
Increased recycling of construction and demolition waste, Demand for higher-quality aggregates with precise gradation, Adoption of modular screens for quick changeovers in multi-product plants, and Integration of automation and remote monitoring in quarry operations.
Representative participants:
Metso Corporation, Sandvik AB, Haver & Boecker OHG, Terex Corporation, and Astec Industries, Inc.
Recycling and Waste Management (estimated share: 15%)
In recycling and waste management, modular screen units are used to separate and classify materials such as plastics, metals, and construction debris. The segment is expanding as regulations push for higher recycling rates and as the circular economy gains traction. Modular screens are ideal for these applications because they can be quickly reconfigured to handle different material streams, improving operational flexibility. The demand for recycled aggregates and secondary raw materials is rising, driven by environmental policies and corporate sustainability goals. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from innovations in screen media that enhance separation efficiency and reduce contamination. Key demand indicators include recycling rates, waste generation volumes, and government targets for material recovery. Major companies in this space include Derrick Corporation, which offers high-frequency modular screens, and Schenck Process, known for its screening solutions for waste processing. Current trend: Growing emphasis on circular economy and material recovery boosts modular screen adoption.
Major trends:
Increasing regulatory pressure for higher recycling rates, Adoption of modular screens for flexible material sorting, Development of wear-resistant media for abrasive recycled materials, and Integration of sensor-based sorting with modular screening systems.
Representative participants:
Derrick Corporation, Schenck Process Holding GmbH, CP Manufacturing, Inc, Krause Manufacturing, and BHS-Sonthofen GmbH.
Industrial Automation and Instrumentation (estimated share: 6%)
Industrial automation and instrumentation applications use modular screen units for precise particle size classification in manufacturing processes, such as in chemical, food, and pharmaceutical industries. These screens are integrated into automated systems that require consistent performance and minimal downtime. The trend toward Industry 4.0 and smart manufacturing is driving demand for screens with embedded sensors and connectivity, enabling real-time monitoring and predictive maintenance. As automation expands, the need for reliable, modular screening solutions grows. By 2035, this segment is expected to see moderate growth, supported by the increasing adoption of automated quality control and the need for high-precision separation. Key indicators include industrial automation spending and the adoption of smart manufacturing technologies. Major companies include Russell Finex, which offers modular screening systems for fine powders, and Sweco, known for its separation equipment. Current trend: Use of modular screens in automated sorting and quality control systems.
Major trends:
Integration of IoT and predictive maintenance in screening equipment, Demand for high-precision separation in pharmaceutical and chemical processing, Adoption of modular designs for easy cleaning and changeover, and Growth of automated quality control systems in manufacturing.
Representative participants:
Russell Finex Ltd, Sweco (M-I SWACO), Kason Corporation, GEA Group AG, and Bühler AG.
OEM Integration and Maintenance (estimated share: 4%)
OEMs of vibrating screens and crushing equipment often supply modular screen units as original equipment or as replacement parts. This segment is driven by the installed base of screening machines and the need for compatible, high-performance media. OEMs are increasingly bundling modular screens with their equipment to ensure optimal performance and to capture aftermarket revenue. The trend toward longer equipment warranties and service contracts is supporting demand for OEM-branded modular panels. Through 2035, the segment will grow in line with the overall market, as OEMs expand their aftermarket offerings and as operators prefer genuine parts for reliability. Key indicators include the global fleet of vibrating screens and the age of installed equipment. Major companies in this segment include Metso, Sandvik, and FLSmidth, which offer comprehensive screening solutions including modular media. Current trend: OEMs increasingly offer modular screen units as part of original equipment and aftermarket packages.
Major trends:
Growth of aftermarket service contracts and performance guarantees, OEMs offering modular screens as part of integrated solutions, Development of proprietary connector systems for quick installation, and Increasing use of digital platforms for ordering and inventory management.
Representative participants:
Metso Corporation, Sandvik AB, FLSmidth & Co. A/S, Terex Corporation, and Astec Industries, Inc.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 42%)
Asia-Pacific dominates the market, driven by massive mining and infrastructure activity in China, India, and Australia. China's steel and coal sectors, along with India's expanding aggregates industry, fuel demand. Australia's iron ore and gold mines are major consumers. Growth is supported by increasing automation and the shift to polymer screens. The region also hosts key manufacturers, contributing to supply. Direction: up.
North America (estimated share: 24%)
North America is a mature market with steady demand from mining (copper, gold, and aggregates) and recycling. The U.S. and Canada have a large installed base of vibrating screens, driving replacement demand. Environmental regulations favor rubber and polyurethane screens. The market is characterized by high adoption of advanced technologies and a strong presence of major producers like Polydeck and Derrick. Direction: stable.
Europe (estimated share: 18%)
Europe's market is driven by aggregates, recycling, and industrial automation. Strict environmental and noise regulations accelerate the adoption of rubber and composite screens. Germany, Sweden, and Finland are key markets with strong mining and construction sectors. The region is a hub for innovation in screen media, with companies like Multotec and Haver & Boecker. Growth is moderate but steady. Direction: stable.
Latin America (estimated share: 9%)
Latin America, led by Chile, Peru, and Brazil, is a growing market due to copper and iron ore mining. The region is import-dependent, with significant cross-border sourcing from North America and Europe. Replacement cycles are short due to abrasive ores. Infrastructure development and mining expansion are key drivers. Local distributors play a crucial role in supply, but logistics remain a challenge. Direction: up.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 7%)
The Middle East & Africa region is emerging, with South Africa, Ghana, and the UAE showing potential. Mining (gold, platinum, and aggregates) and infrastructure projects drive demand. The region relies heavily on imports, with long lead times and high logistics costs. However, growing investment in mining and construction is expected to boost the market. Local manufacturing is limited, offering opportunities for international suppliers. Direction: up.

ESD Safe Trays Market to Reach Index 192 by 2035 on Semiconductor Fab Build-Out
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
ESD Safe Trays market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global ESD safe trays market is set to expand at a compound annual growth rate of 6.8% from 2026 to 2035, with market value indexed at 192 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by the relentless expansion of semiconductor fabrication capacity, the proliferation of miniaturized electronic components, and the tightening of electrostatic discharge (ESD) control regulations across manufacturing hubs. As electronics become denser and more sensitive, the demand for precision-engineered trays that ensure safe handling, storage, and transport is intensifying. The market is also benefiting from the shift toward application-specific designs, including RFID-integrated trays, collapsible modular systems, and high-temperature carbon-fiber-loaded variants, which now account for over 40% of global revenue. These specialty products command average selling prices 25–35% above standard trays, offering manufacturers higher margin stability. Supply chain geography remains heavily skewed toward Asia-Pacific, which hosts over 55% of world demand and an estimated 60–65% of precision injection-molding capacity dedicated to ESD packaging. However, the market faces challenges from volatile polymer resin prices, lengthy qualification cycles, and the high capital intensity of advanced tooling. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of market size, demand structure, supply capability, trade flows, pricing, and competitive landscape, with a forecast horizon extending to 2035.
The baseline scenario for the ESD safe trays market through 2035 points to steady, above-average growth, driven by structural demand from semiconductor fabrication, automotive electronics, and the broader electronics assembly ecosystem. The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 6.8% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching 192 by 2035 relative to 2025. This growth is supported by the ongoing global build-out of wafer fabrication plants, particularly in the United States, Europe, and Southeast Asia, which is creating sustained demand for high-precision ESD trays. Additionally, the transition to electric vehicles and advanced driver-assistance systems is increasing the electronic content per vehicle, further boosting demand for static-safe handling solutions. The market is also witnessing a shift toward sustainable materials, with recycled and bio-based conductive polymers gaining traction, albeit with performance validation hurdles. Near-shoring and regionalization of electronics assembly are prompting suppliers to establish local molding operations, particularly in Mexico, Eastern Europe, and Southeast Asia, to reduce lead times and freight costs. However, the market faces restraints including volatility in specialty polymer resin prices, particularly for carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube loaded compounds, which compresses margins and complicates long-term procurement contracts. Qualification cycles for new suppliers in semiconductor and automotive sectors often extend 12–18 months, creating high entry barriers. Furthermore, increasingly intricate tray geometries for next-generation components push the limits of injection molding tolerance and tooling economics, elevating upfront capital requirements and favoring larger, technically equipped molders. Primary Demand Drivers

Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Electronics Assembly and Semiconductor Handling (estimated share: 45%)
This segment is the largest consumer of ESD safe trays, driven by the global expansion of semiconductor fabrication plants and the increasing complexity of electronic components. As chip geometries shrink and device densities rise, the need for trays that prevent static damage during handling, storage, and transport becomes more critical. The segment is witnessing a shift from standard trays to custom-designed solutions that integrate features like RFID tracking, high-temperature resistance, and precise cavity tolerances. Demand-side indicators include semiconductor capital expenditure, wafer starts, and the adoption of automated material handling systems in fabs. Through 2035, growth will be supported by the construction of new fabs in the US, Europe, and Southeast Asia, as well as the continued miniaturization of electronics. The trend toward 300mm wafer handling and advanced packaging technologies will further drive the need for specialized trays. Major players in this segment are investing in R&D to develop trays that meet the stringent cleanliness and static dissipation requirements of next-generation semiconductor processes. Current trend: Increasing demand for high-precision, application-specific trays for wafer and component handling.
Major trends:
Integration of RFID and IoT sensors for real-time tracking, High-temperature carbon-fiber-loaded compounds for demanding processes, Modular and collapsible designs for efficient return logistics, and Custom cavity geometries for advanced packaging and 3D stacking.
Representative participants:
RTP Company, Teknis Limited, Conductive Containers Inc, Polymer Molding Inc, and Mishima Kosan Co., Ltd.
Automotive Electronics and EV Components (estimated share: 20%)
The automotive sector is a fast-growing end-user of ESD safe trays, driven by the electrification of vehicles and the increasing electronic content per car. Electric vehicles contain significantly more semiconductors and sensitive electronic modules than conventional vehicles, including battery management systems, power inverters, and ADAS sensors. These components require static-safe handling throughout the supply chain, from component manufacturing to final assembly. The segment is seeing a shift toward trays that can withstand higher temperatures and provide better protection for larger, heavier components. Demand-side indicators include EV production volumes, automotive semiconductor content, and the localization of battery and electronics manufacturing. Through 2035, the growth of EV sales, particularly in China, Europe, and North America, will drive sustained demand for ESD trays. Additionally, the trend toward modular vehicle platforms and the integration of electronics into structural components will create new requirements for custom tray designs. Suppliers are working closely with automotive OEMs and tier-1 suppliers to develop trays that meet the rigorous quality and reliability standards of the industry. Current trend: Rapid growth in electric vehicle production and advanced driver-assistance systems.
Major trends:
High-temperature resistant materials for under-hood applications, Custom trays for battery cells and power modules, Integration with automated assembly and robotic handling, and Compliance with automotive industry quality standards (IATF 16949).
Representative participants:
Nefab AB, GWP Group, Elcom (UK) Ltd, ITW EAE, and Totech Corporation.
Industrial and B2B Manufacturing (estimated share: 15%)
This segment encompasses a broad range of industrial applications, including the production of industrial electronics, medical devices, aerospace components, and telecommunications equipment. These industries handle static-sensitive components that require ESD protection during manufacturing, testing, and logistics. The demand for ESD safe trays in this segment is driven by the increasing automation of production lines, which requires standardized and stackable trays for efficient material flow. The segment is also benefiting from the trend toward Industry 4.0, where trays are integrated with sensors and tracking systems to enable real-time inventory management. Demand-side indicators include industrial production indices, automation investment, and the growth of the medical device and aerospace sectors. Through 2035, the segment is expected to grow steadily, supported by the reshoring of manufacturing activities and the expansion of high-tech industries in emerging markets. The need for trays that can withstand harsh environments, such as high humidity or temperature variations, is also increasing, driving demand for specialty materials and coatings. Current trend: Steady demand from general electronics manufacturing and industrial automation.
Major trends:
Adoption of Industry 4.0 and smart factory solutions, Use of conductive and static-dissipative materials with enhanced durability, Custom trays for medical devices and aerospace components, and Integration with automated storage and retrieval systems.
Representative participants:
Conductive Containers Inc, RTP Company, Brick Packaging, Antistatic Industries, and Nefab AB.
Retail and E-commerce Packaging (estimated share: 10%)
The rise of e-commerce has created new demand for ESD safe trays in the retail and distribution of electronic components and consumer electronics. Online marketplaces and distributors require packaging that protects sensitive components from static damage during shipping and handling. This segment includes trays used for the packaging of memory modules, processors, and other components sold directly to consumers or small businesses. The demand is driven by the growth of online electronics sales, the increasing popularity of DIY electronics and repair, and the need for secure and tamper-evident packaging. Through 2035, the segment is expected to grow as e-commerce continues to expand globally, particularly in emerging markets. The trend toward sustainable packaging is also influencing this segment, with a growing preference for recyclable and reusable trays. However, the cost sensitivity of retail packaging may limit the adoption of high-end specialty trays, favoring standard and cost-effective solutions. Current trend: Growing demand for ESD-safe packaging in online sales of electronic components.
Major trends:
E-commerce growth driving demand for protective packaging, Sustainable and recyclable tray materials, Tamper-evident and anti-static features, and Custom branding and labeling for retail channels.
Representative participants:
GWP Group, Elcom (UK) Ltd, Brick Packaging, and Antistatic Industries.
Foodservice and Institutional (estimated share: 10%)
This segment includes the use of ESD safe trays in foodservice and institutional settings where static control is necessary, such as cleanrooms, laboratories, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. In these environments, trays are used to handle sensitive electronic components, medical devices, and pharmaceutical products that require protection from static discharge. The demand is driven by the growth of the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors, as well as the increasing stringency of cleanroom standards. Through 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a moderate pace, supported by the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and the increasing use of automation in laboratories. The demand for trays that can withstand chemical exposure and sterilization processes is also rising, driving the use of specialized materials. However, the segment is relatively small compared to others, and growth may be limited by the niche nature of applications. Current trend: Niche but stable demand for ESD-safe trays in cleanroom and laboratory environments.
Major trends:
Cleanroom-compatible materials and certifications, Chemical resistance and sterilizability, Integration with laboratory automation systems, and Compliance with pharmaceutical and healthcare standards.
Representative participants:
Teknis Limited, Conductive Containers Inc, Nefab AB, and ITW EAE.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 55%)
Asia-Pacific remains the largest market, driven by semiconductor manufacturing in Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China, as well as the rapid expansion of electronics assembly in Southeast Asia. The region hosts over 60% of global precision injection-molding capacity for ESD packaging. Growth is supported by government investments in semiconductor fabs and the relocation of supply chains. Direction: Dominant and fastest-growing.
North America (estimated share: 20%)
North America is experiencing a resurgence in semiconductor manufacturing, with new fabs under construction in the US. The region also has a strong automotive electronics sector, particularly in Mexico. Demand is driven by the CHIPS Act and the trend toward near-shoring. The market is characterized by high adoption of advanced tray technologies and stringent ESD standards. Direction: Steady growth.
Europe (estimated share: 15%)
Europe is focusing on increasing its semiconductor production capacity, with investments in Germany, France, and the Netherlands. The automotive industry, a major user of ESD trays, is transitioning to EVs, boosting demand. The region also has a strong presence of specialty tray manufacturers and a growing emphasis on sustainable materials. Direction: Moderate growth.
Latin America (estimated share: 5%)
Latin America, led by Mexico, is becoming a key hub for electronics assembly and automotive manufacturing, attracting investments from global companies. The demand for ESD safe trays is growing as local supply chains develop. However, the market is still relatively small, with limited local production capacity, leading to reliance on imports. Direction: Emerging growth.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 5%)
The Middle East and Africa are gradually developing their electronics and industrial sectors, with investments in smart manufacturing and infrastructure. The demand for ESD safe trays is limited but growing, particularly in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and South Africa. The market is heavily import-dependent, with opportunities for suppliers offering cost-effective solutions. Direction: Slow but steady.

Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Semiconductor and Precision Manufacturing (estimated share: 45%)
The semiconductor sector is the largest consumer of submicron filter cartridges, driven by the need to maintain yields above 95% in advanced fabrication. As process nodes shrink to 7nm and below, the tolerance for particulate contamination decreases exponentially, requiring filters with absolute removal ratings of 0.003-0.05 µm. These filters are used in wet processing, CMP, lithography, and gas delivery systems. The demand is closely tied to wafer starts, which are projected to grow at a CAGR of 5-7% through 2035, supported by government incentives and the proliferation of AI and 5G chips. The replacement cycle for point-of-use filters is 12-18 months, creating a steady aftermarket. Key demand indicators include fab utilization rates, capital expenditure by major foundries, and the adoption of EUV lithography. By 2035, the sector is expected to account for 45% of global demand, with growth driven by the expansion of memory and logic fabs in Asia-Pacific and the US. Current trend: Increasing demand for sub-0.05 µm absolute-rated cartridges for EUV and advanced node processes.
Major trends:
Shift toward EUV lithography requiring finer filtration, Adoption of smart sensors for real-time filter monitoring, Increased use of PTFE membranes for chemical compatibility, and Localization of supply chains to reduce lead times.
Representative participants:
Entegris Inc, Pall Corporation, Merck KGaA, Donaldson Company Inc, and Parker Hannifin Corporation.
Electronics and Optical Systems (estimated share: 20%)
The electronics and optical systems segment relies on submicron filter cartridges to maintain clean environments for producing flat panel displays, LEDs, and optical lenses. These applications require filtration of process chemicals and gases to prevent defects from particles and bubbles. The demand is driven by the expansion of OLED and micro-LED production, particularly in South Korea and China. As display resolutions increase, the need for finer filtration becomes critical. The segment is also influenced by the growth of augmented reality and virtual reality devices, which require high-quality optical components. The replacement cycle for filters in this segment is typically 12-24 months, depending on the process. By 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5-8%, supported by the increasing adoption of advanced display technologies and the miniaturization of optical systems. Current trend: Growing demand for high-purity filtration in flat panel display and optical component manufacturing.
Major trends:
Rising production of OLED and micro-LED displays, Demand for ultra-pure water in display manufacturing, Integration of filtration with process control systems, and Growth in AR/VR device manufacturing.
Representative participants:
3M Company, Pall Corporation, Entegris Inc, Sartorius AG, and Cobetter Filtration Equipment Co. Ltd.
Industrial Automation and Instrumentation (estimated share: 15%)
Industrial automation and instrumentation applications require submicron filter cartridges to protect sensitive equipment from particulate contamination in hydraulic fluids, lubricants, and process gases. The growth of Industry 4.0 and the increasing automation of manufacturing processes are driving demand for reliable filtration to ensure equipment uptime and product quality. The segment includes applications in robotics, CNC machines, and analytical instruments. The demand is also supported by the need for consistent performance in harsh environments. The replacement cycle for filters in this segment is typically 6-12 months, depending on operating conditions. By 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 4-6%, driven by the expansion of smart factories and the increasing complexity of automated systems. Current trend: Increasing use of submicron filters in precision instrumentation and automated manufacturing processes.
Major trends:
Adoption of predictive maintenance in industrial equipment, Integration of filters with IoT sensors, Demand for high-efficiency filters in hydraulic systems, and Growth of automated manufacturing in emerging economies.
Representative participants:
Parker Hannifin Corporation, Donaldson Company Inc, Eaton Corporation, 3M Company, and Porvair Filtration Group.
OEM Integration and Maintenance (estimated share: 12%)
OEMs in the semiconductor, pharmaceutical, and food and beverage industries increasingly integrate submicron filter cartridges into their equipment, creating a steady demand for both initial fit and replacement parts. This segment includes the supply of cartridges to equipment manufacturers, as well as maintenance and replacement services. The demand is driven by the need for seamless integration and performance guarantees. OEMs often specify particular filter brands and models, creating long-term supply relationships. The aftermarket segment is particularly attractive due to recurring revenue and higher margins. The replacement cycle varies by application, but for critical processes, it can be as short as 3-6 months. By 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 6-8%, supported by the increasing complexity of equipment and the need for specialized filtration solutions. Current trend: Rising demand for integrated filtration systems and aftermarket services from OEMs.
Major trends:
Long-term supply agreements with OEMs, Growth of aftermarket services and consumables, Customization of filters for specific equipment, and Digital platforms for filter monitoring and replacement.
Representative participants:
Entegris Inc, Pall Corporation, Merck KGaA, Sartorius AG, and Critical Process Filtration Inc.
Pharmaceutical and Bioprocessing (estimated share: 8%)
The pharmaceutical and bioprocessing sector is a growing end-user of submicron filter cartridges, particularly for sterile filtration of drugs, vaccines, and biologics. The demand is driven by the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing capacity, especially for monoclonal antibodies and cell and gene therapies. These applications require filters with absolute ratings of 0.1-0.2 µm to remove bacteria and particulates while maintaining product integrity. The segment is also influenced by regulatory requirements for sterility assurance. The replacement cycle for filters in this segment is typically 1-2 years, depending on batch sizes and product characteristics. By 2035, the segment is expected to grow at a CAGR of 7-9%, supported by the increasing investment in biopharma manufacturing and the development of personalized medicines. Current trend: Increasing adoption of submicron filters for sterile filtration and contamination control in biopharma manufacturing.
Major trends:
Growth of single-use technologies in bioprocessing, Increasing demand for sterilizing-grade filters, Adoption of disposable filter cartridges, and Expansion of biopharma manufacturing in Asia-Pacific.
Representative participants:
Sartorius AG, Pall Corporation, Merck KGaA, 3M Company, and Porvair Filtration Group.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 65%)
Asia-Pacific leads the market with 65% share, driven by semiconductor fabs in Taiwan, South Korea, China, Japan, and Singapore. The region's growth is supported by massive investments in advanced node capacity and cleanroom expansions. Demand is expected to grow at a CAGR of 7-10% through 2035, with China and India emerging as key manufacturing hubs. Direction: Dominant and fastest-growing region.
North America (estimated share: 18%)
North America holds 18% share, supported by the CHIPS Act and the expansion of domestic semiconductor manufacturing. The region is also a leader in pharmaceutical and bioprocessing filtration. Growth is projected at 5-7% CAGR, with increasing demand for high-efficiency filters in advanced packaging and R&D facilities. Direction: Steady growth with reshoring initiatives.
Europe (estimated share: 12%)
Europe accounts for 12% of the market, with strong demand from automotive electronics and pharmaceutical sectors. The region is emphasizing sustainable filtration solutions and circular economy practices. Growth is expected at 4-6% CAGR, with Germany and France leading in innovation and adoption of smart filtration systems. Direction: Moderate growth with focus on sustainability.
Latin America (estimated share: 3%)
Latin America represents 3% of the market, with growth driven by the expansion of food and beverage and pharmaceutical industries. Brazil and Mexico are key markets, but the region faces infrastructure challenges. Growth is projected at 3-5% CAGR, with increasing foreign investment in manufacturing. Direction: Emerging market with gradual expansion.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 2%)
The Middle East and Africa account for 2% of the market, with demand primarily from oil and gas and water treatment sectors. The region is investing in industrial diversification, which may create opportunities for filtration suppliers. Growth is expected at 2-4% CAGR, with UAE and Saudi Arabia leading. Direction: Niche market with selective opportunities.
